subject: Operator telemetry, escrow options, and key custody clarifications for on-prem appliance
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <security@helixmed.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operator telemetry & escrow approach for on-prem appliance

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helix is very interested in Redwood Private for an upcoming diagnostic workloads rollout. Before we proceed to procurement we need to clarify a few privacy/security items for our legal and infosec teams. High-level asks: 

- Confirm whether any operator telemetry or logs from customer on-prem appliances could contain customer data (PHI/PII) in plaintext. If so, what redaction or sampling policies exist?
- We need a description of any operator access paths (SSH, operator console, support sessions) and whether these require any key material held by Redwood.
- For key custody: can Redwood support a split-key escrow model where Helix controls a portion of the key and Redwood uses a sealed HSM/escrow for recovery? 
- Who are the subprocessors involved in Private appliance support and where are they located (cross-border transfers)?

Can you please provide a short write-up and attach any relevant DPA/redline excerpts? Our procurement team needs that to finalize the SOW.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Regards,
Daniel Kim
Security Engineering
Helix Medical Systems

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <security@helixmed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator telemetry & escrow approach for on-prem appliance

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (legal) and Aditya (product) to cover contractual language and the technical options.

Quick answers up front:
- Operator telemetry can be configured to avoid any customer payload capture; default telemetry is health/metrics only.
- Redwood operators do not need to possess plaintext customer data to provide support; we use obfuscated traces and customer-provided debugging snapshots.
- We support customer-controlled keys and have two escrow patterns we commonly propose: split-key escrow with a neutral third-party escrow, or attested HSM sealing where only a customer-initiated unseal returns keys.

See Monica's notes and Aditya's technical summary below. I attached our current DPA redline for reference.

Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[attachment: dpa_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Daniel Kim <security@helixmed.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator telemetry & escrow approach for on-prem appliance

Daniel / team — adding legal context and suggested DPA language. Please consider these as negotiation starting points: 

1) Telemetry: Redwood will limit support telemetry to non-content metrics by default (CPU, process health, paged-errors). If customers enable deeper debugging traces, such traces are only retained for a max of 30 days and are redacted by pattern-based scrubbers before being accessible to Redwood staff. Proposed clause: 
"Redwood agrees that support telemetry from on-prem appliances will exclude customer payloads by default; any customer-authorized debug traces may be collected only with prior written approval and will be redacted and retained no longer than 30 days."

2) Key custody / escrow: we can offer two contractable options — (A) Customer-Held Primary Key + Redwood Recovery Key held in split escrow (2-of-3 with a neutral escrow service), or (B) Customer-Held Key sealed in an attested HSM; Redwood holds no copy of plaintext key material. Proposed addendum: key custody appendix to DPA describing option selection, escrow provider SLAs, and process for emergency breakglass (audit log + customer approval).

3) Operator access: all operator sessions require documented breakglass approvals and are recorded; operator accounts are limited to support-bound actions and are audited. Add clause for notification windows and audit log retention.

4) Subprocessors & transfers: Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and notify Helix of substantive changes 30 days prior. We accept reasoned geo-fencing requests where feasible; cross-border transfers will be limited per agreed scope in the DPA.

I've attached a redline that highlights where these clauses can be inserted. We should align on which key custody option Helix prefers so we can produce the SOW language.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[attachment: dpa_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <security@helixmed.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: operator telemetry & escrow approach for on-prem appliance

Hi Daniel — technical clarifications from product/ops side to help you evaluate options: 

- Telemetry details: By default, the appliance emits aggregated metrics (prometheus style counters, health-heartbeats, disk/memory usage). No request/response payloads are shipped. For debug mode we capture a trace that includes headers and partial payload only when explicitly turned on by the customer; that mode is off by default and requires a signed activation token from the customer.

- Key options: 
  Option 1 — Split-key escrow: Helix holds key shares (e.g., 2-of-3 scheme) where Redwood holds an operational share that cannot decrypt without combining with customer share(s) and the neutral escrow. Recovery requires a documented process with two-party approvals.
  Option 2 — Attested HSM sealing: Keys are provisioned into a tamper-resistant HSM (on-prem appliance), sealed via remote attestation. Redwood operators cannot export plaintext keys; the HSM will only unseal to a customer-approved identity.

- Breakglass: for emergency support we can implement a mutual action workflow: 1) Helix initiates breakglass request in portal; 2) request is logged and triggers an automated notification to Helix admins; 3) support session is time-limited and recorded; 4) post-session artifacts (audit logs) are delivered to Helix and stored for X days. We can add a configurable 24-hour post-session retention for logs on customer side only.

- Subprocessors (current): managed-hardware-provider@example.com (US), remote-support-tooling@example.com (EU). We will provide a CSV of the subprocessor list and locations.

Link to internal design doc (read-only): https://redwood-drive.internal/rdw/private-appliance-design-v2 — this includes HSM attestation flows and escrow integration notes.

If Helix wants the split-key escrow we can draft the appendix tying to an escrow vendor; we typically recommend using a neutral escrow with certified controls.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Olga / Monica / Aditya — thanks for the detailed responses and the redline. This addresses most of our concerns. A few next steps from Helix: 

- We prefer Option 1 (split-key escrow) with a neutral escrow provider. Please propose 2–3 escrow vendors and their SLAs.
- We need the DPA appendix with the breakglass workflow and telemetry redaction language included in the SOW draft.
- Please provide the current subprocessor CSV (as mentioned) and confirm no subprocessors outside US/EU will be used for support.

Let's schedule a 30-min call next week to lock the SOW language and escrow vendor list — Tuesdays or Wednesdays morning PT work best for our team.
